depression, recurrent UTI (urethral diverticulum) and obesity

She was discharged only 5 days ago after admission for a 
gastroparesis flare which was treated symptomatically. She now 
presents with two days of her characteristic gastroparesis pain 
which has resulted in inability to tolerate PO and 4 episodes of 
NBNB emesis.

Initial exam notable for pt moaning in pain  
Meds administered - 2LNS; metoclopramide 10mg IV; ketorolac 20mg 
IV; acetaminophen 1g IV  
On admission to the floor, she continues to have severe adminal 
pain. She tells me that after her recent discharge she was well 
for only 2 days but then had recurrence of her chronic symptoms. 
She normally eats a ""whole grain diet"" which her daughter 
prepares for her at home, but states she has been unable to 
tolerate PO for the past 2 days due to pain and unabating 
nausea. She has had no change in her bowel movements (i.e. 
formed, daily stools which are dark ___ Fe supplementation). Her 
___ at home have been 100s-200s; she took only 4U of short-acting 
insulin today at lunch (broth).  
She was previously followed at ___ and only recently transferred 
care her to ___. She tells me that she was hospitalized at ___ 
>1 monthly ""for the past ___ years"" for both gastroparesis and 
HHS/DKA (DKA hospitalizations are ""too many to count""). She 
denies that any medical intervention has ever truly helped her 
symptoms. In regard to her transfer of care, she states ""I just 
got tired of them sending me home sick. They kept giving me pain 
and nausea medications but I was still sick."" She denies having 
previously been on maintenance opiates for pain control, citing 
the fact that ___ physicians were reluctant to give pain 
medication due to the potential for worsening gastric motility.  

Her care at ___ begins 3 months ago. Initially she was seen in 
the ED x 2 for abdominal pain (___) and discharged home 
from the ED after being treated with tramadol. Since then, she 
has been admitted for abdominal pain with most ED presentations. 
This is her ___ admission in the past 2 months, summarized in 
reverse chronological order as follows:  
___: gastroparesis flare; treated symptomatically with 
minmal opiates; also treated for uncomplicated cystitis although 
UCx ultimately demonstrated only contamination  
___: gastroparesis flare; treated symptomatically with 
minimal opiates  
___: severe abdominal pain and inability to take PO; 
admitted to MICU with hypertensive emergency (demonstrated by 
AMS), treated with bolus labetalol  
___: RUQ and flank pain, presumed ___ pyelonephritis. 
UCx demonstrated fecal contamination. Treated w/ 2 week course

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year-old woman with longstanding type 2 diabetes mellitus 
(complicated by gastroparesis, neuropathy, proteinuria without 
significantly impaired GFR), hypertension, depression, and 
obesity presenting with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain.

# GASTROPARESIS FLARE: The patient presented with epigastric 
abdominal ___ consistent with prior episodes of gastroparesis 
flare. The patient was treated with ondansetron PRN and home 
metaclopromide for nausea, Tylenol and Tramadol for pain, with 
improvement in her symptoms. She was able to tolerate a full 
meal prior to discharge. Educated the patient the the long-term 
solution to gastroparesis is strict control of diabetes and 
small meals.

# TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS: Patient diagnosed at age ___, now 
with complications of gastroparesis, neuropathy, and 
nephropathy.  Found during this admission to have A1c 8.3% on 
home insulin. While patient was NPO, she was placed on lowered 
dose (20 units instead of 35 units of QHS lantus) with low-dose 
insulin sliding scale without complications.  She was instructed 
to resume her home insulin regimen on discharge. 

# HYPERTENSION: During this admission, the patient's blood 
pressure was found to be elevated with systolics 150-180s. This 
was likely in the setting of gastroparesis/abdominal pain. Her 
home regimen of lisinopril and nifedipine were continued without 
complications.  

# LEUKOCYTOSIS/THROMBOCYTOSIS: In ___ system, patient has had 
persistent leukocytosis, anemia, and thrombocytosis without a 
clear identified infection. In the setting of multiple 
admissions for gastroparesis flares, this could represent a 
response. Would recommend rechecking CBC as an outpatient and 
consider peripheral smear and Hematology consult if leukocytosis 
and thrombocytosis persist.

==============================

==============================
MEDICATIONS
- STARTED on ondansetron Q8H:PRN nausea
- Continued home metaclopramide, but recommend discontinuing as 
soon as possible given risk for extrapyridamal side effects

- Would recommend rechecking CBC as an outpatient and consider
